name: N. Rangasamy
role: Puducherry chief minister and founder of the All India N. R. Congress
summary: Rangasamy combines extensive welfare provision with investment promotion and a pragmatic alliance strategy aimed at obtaining central government support. He seeks full statehood for Puducherry, describes his party as secular, and supports public spending on cultural heritage and religious institutions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His 2024 budget proposes exempting small and medium enterprises from licences and inspections for their first three production years.

cut-welfare.rationale: His 2026 budget reports increased pensions and women’s monthly assistance and promises continued expansion of welfare coverage.

decide-locally.rationale: He demands full elected state authority for Puducherry, objecting to administrative dependence on the centrally appointed lieutenant governor.

more-religion-public.rationale: His 2025 budget increases recurring temple assistance and repair funding; his earlier programme also advertises public assistance for mosque renovation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His 2026 budget proposes a World Tamil Conference and a university chair to preserve and enrich Tamil linguistic heritage.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His 2026 budget supports a permanent climate-change cell, a low-carbon growth strategy and a major coastal resilience project.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His 2024 budget proposes an industrial estate and deployment of idle public-enterprise land for IT, research and financial-technology facilities.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He explains alignment with the central ruling party as a practical strategy for development, describing such support as necessary to get things done.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His 2011 speech called for proper implementation of funds for disadvantaged communities; his 2024 budget explicitly prioritises marginalised and vulnerable residents.

socialized-care.rationale: His 2026 budget commits to strengthened public Anganwadi services, improved centres and increased payments to their workers and helpers.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He expanded government hospitals in his earlier administration and proposes further investment in public primary-health facilities, demonstrating support for a continuing public provider role.

farm-price-support.rationale: His 2025 budget promises Minimum Support Price arrangements for diversified crops through PM-AASHA.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He combines income-tested aid for women with food distribution to all ration-card holders, rather than consistently choosing targeting or universality.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: In 2011 he explicitly committed his party to secular principles and politics above caste, religion or creed.

notes: Reviewed all 490 statements against records from 2001–2008 and the 2011 campaign, the 2024–2027 budget speeches and recent interviews. Government budget announcements are identified as proposals or reported implementation, not independent proof of delivery. No national or foreign-policy position is imputed from his BJP alliance. Statehood means an Indian state, not independence; it does not establish a right to secede. He said electricity privatisation remained undecided and before the courts in 2024; later criticism by opponents is not treated as his own endorsement. General secularism does not establish a position on specific religious dress, blasphemy or marriage laws. Full fee aid to particular disadvantaged groups is not universal free college. Digital administration is not support for algorithmic rule or online political voting. Reservations concerning caste or government schooling do not establish a racial theory.
